minutes.headline: Charter Review Committee dropped the registered-voter rule for appointees and set January to April hearing dates.
minutes.summary: The committee welcomed new members, chose officers and approved the prior minutes. It debated write-in thresholds and whether appointees must be registered voters. It then voted on purple and brown charter changes, including a calendar-day definition, and left the red items for the public hearing. It set a schedule of hearings and meetings through April.

public_comment.topic: Asked the committee to consider wording so the Park Commission could be three or five members, matching state law chapter 45.
Objected to requiring registered voters for appointments to committees and urged language allowing any resident to serve.
Said requiring registered voters could exclude potential members, even from this committee.
Asked whether resident of Lunenburg was in the eligibility wording for appointees.
Suggested reviewing all appointed boards, including this committee, for registered-voter standards, and noted resident could include high school students.

Accept the brown planning director language.
Approve the brown town manager personnel language.
Accept screening committee language, amended to town residents.
Approve the brown bargaining unit language.
Accept the brown filling vacancies language.
Accept the town manager compliance language as written.

decisions.decision: The clerk will go through the document and change day references to calendar days, marking them brown, with exceptions.
Red items will not be voted on tonight and will go to the public hearing as open questions.
Public hearing set for January 9 at Town Hall.
Second public hearing set for February 27; meeting on March 13.
Proposed changes will be posted online before and after the public hearing, subject to legal review.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to remove the brown appointment language in 3-2-D, keeping the Finance Committee registered-voter wording; the vote was announced as 7-1.
It voted to define a day as a calendar day except where stated otherwise, and to change references to months into 30-day counts.
It approved the purple changes except those referring to days or months, and accepted the changes in 4-5 and the town manager compliance language as written.
Red items were not voted on and go to the public hearing as open questions.
A public hearing was set for January 9 at Town Hall, a second for February 27, and a meeting for March 13.

why_it_matters: The changes shape who can be appointed to Lunenburg boards and how charter deadlines are counted, and the committee's final package is what residents will later be asked to vote on.
The red items are still open, so residents can weigh in on them at the public hearing before the committee decides.
watch_next: Public hearing on January 9 at Town Hall, then a second hearing on February 27 and a committee meeting on March 13.
Proposed changes are to be posted online before and after the public hearing, subject to legal review.

The records agree on the main motions: the day and month definitions, the purple items, the 7-1 vote on 3-2(d) and 4-5. Our minutes leave about ten votes with no outcome ("not audible"), and the official minutes record the passed votes with 8-0 tallies.
The main thing to know is that the section numbers and wording of the later votes are hard to line up between the two records. Check the recording for those votes, for the first public hearing date, for the March 13 meeting, and for who was assigned to edit the day references.
